messages.subject: Two naive rattle questions
messages.body_plain:
1. Running on ubuntu 9.04 (64bit), rattle 2.5.47 saving to png is
behaving poorly. Have I configured something incorrectly? I'd post a
picture of the "breakage" (checkerboard black/white across the entire
image) but I don't see how to add attachments to the forum, sorry.

   2. Using the "edit" feature which is clearly implemented via
RGtk2Dfedit ... I can change the "column" title I want to edit, but it
doesn't seem to propagate to the rattle environment and I'm at a loss
to see how to "save" when the RGtk2Dfedit online documentation says
it's automatically propagated ... either I've missed something, or
installed things incorrectly.

Hints to which bits of the documentation I should read more carefully
gratefully accepted!

messages.subject: Re: two naive rattle questions
messages.body_plain:
I came across this graphics question the other day in R (Rattle not running) cutting & pasting into PowerPoint slides. Copying as a metafile did indeed make the background transparent. So I ended up with black lines & points on a dark gray background (the slides themselves). They were impossible to read. So I switched to "Copy as Image", the equivalent to a png file, which took along a white background and looked much better on the slides. When printing of course, the png would have to be pretty densly done (600 dpi?) to not look jagged.

Cheers,
Bob Muenchen

http://r4stats.com

messages.subject: Re: a new question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Albert,

Im not sure if this is the correct answer to your issue, but both Graham and I had problems installing 2.11 and getting the windows R console to work.

I think it tries to open an previous working file, without the correct packages running, and hence, it fails and errors out.

My work around was to go to the R Bin directory, locate a program called RTerm.exe and run it,. This bring up a R dos terminal console, and then i run the

> install.packages("rattle",
dependencies=c("Depends", "Suggests"))

from grahams togaware windows webpage.

Grahams work around is to put the cursor on the windows icon and press right mouse button and then

Right mouse click on the R 2.11.1 icon on your desktop
Delete the "\Documents" from the "Start In" option.

Hopefully either way should work.

It appears that your problem is that no packages are loaded at all.

So either way in the R console or the RTerm.exe you need to install all the packages with the

> install.packages("rattle",
dependencies=c("Depends", "Suggests"))

Hope this works
Regards
Tony
